title: Keya House:
length: about 80 s (about 77 s without the “cut first” row)
headline: Someone in crisis pulls up to a house that looks like every other house. This video shows them what it is like before they walk in.
story: Keya House is a peer-run respite home in Lincoln. You call, you register by phone, and you can stay up to five days with a peer there 24/7. It looks like any other house, and that is the point.

MHA asked for this: show the house the way a first-time guest sees it, and show the art room, so it is clear Keya is not a place to hide in a room. Peers and guests, never clinical. It must feel calm, safe and welcoming.
do: Open on frame 1 on the outside of the house with the hook text.
When a speaker names a thing, cut to that thing: the table, the phone, the art room.
Small name supers, 3 s, the first time each person is on camera.
One text card at “up to five days”: Stay up to 5 days · 24/7 peer support.
Show the art room so it is clear guests are not hiding in a room.
dont: No street number, house number, street sign or address in any frame.
No guest face without a signed release (Amber Pendley holds them; ask Nick).
No Warm Line call clips (C4689–C4693). They belong to the Warm Line video.
No “patient”, “treatment”, “clinic”, “facility” or curfew rules on screen.
No phone number on screen until Nick confirms the Keya number with Madison.
